title: Makeup artistry scope and the skin-penetration boundary
audience: Makeup artists who apply makeup at a client's home, a venue or a studio, and business owners who decide which makeup services to offer
learningOutcomes: Explain why permanent and semi-permanent makeup are outside this course
Decide whether a proposed service is inside the approved service list
Name the check to make before adding any service that may involve skin penetration
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: Department of Health Victoria, Hairdressing and make-up application: infection prevention and control (updated 19 August 2019); Department of Health Victoria, Health guidelines for personal care and body art industries (updated 26 October 2026). Both are listed in full at the end of the lesson.

instruction.heading: What this course covers and what it leaves out
instruction.body: This course covers temporary makeup: applying makeup for events, portraits, photography and everyday wear, at a client's home, a venue or a studio. Permanent makeup and semi-permanent makeup put pigment into the skin, which is skin penetration. Tattooing is also skin penetration. Injectable cosmetic treatments are excluded from this course as well. None of these services is taught here, and no lesson in this course gives authority to offer them. The Victorian Department of Health states that hairdressing and temporary make-up application businesses must follow the Infection prevention and control guidelines for hair, beauty, tattooing and skin penetration industries (2019). That guideline covers the wider group of services, including services that do involve skin penetration. Whether a particular skin-penetration service needs registration, a licence or a council permit depends on the state, territory and council. This course does not set that position, and a student must check it separately before offering any such service.

instruction.heading: Why the service list has to be written down
instruction.body: A therapist or artist who works from a written list of approved services can decline an out-of-scope request without guessing. The list should name each service, the products used for it, the place it is performed, and the date the business last reviewed it. A request for a service that is not on the list is declined, and the decline is recorded. Verbal promises to a client are not a substitute for the list. A service that looks minor, such as a brow shape or a body glitter application, still needs to be checked against the list, because the skin-penetration question depends on what is done to the skin, not on how small the service looks.

instruction.heading: Checking a proposed new service
instruction.body: Before a new service is added, the business owner works through four questions. First, does the service involve breaking the skin, placing pigment or any other substance beneath it, or injecting anything? If yes, it is outside this course. Second, is there a state, territory or council position on that kind of service at the location where it would be done? The answer must be recorded with its source and date. Third, does each product used for the service have a current safety data sheet held by the business? Fourth, has the owner added the service to the approved list with a review date? A service is only offered once all four questions have a recorded answer. If any answer is missing, the service stays off the menu.

procedure: Check the proposed service against the approved service list, and decline any service that is not on it
Confirm the service does not involve skin penetration or injection. If it does, decline it under this course and record the decision
Record the state, territory or council position for the service at the location, with its source and date
Confirm that a current safety data sheet is held for each product the service uses
Add the service to the approved list with a review date, or record why it was declined
Give the client only the information that is on the approved list

workedExamples.situation: A bride asks whether the artist can also apply semi-permanent eyebrow pigment at her home on the morning of the wedding.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the artist say, and what should be recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: Semi-permanent pigment is placed into the skin, so the service involves skin penetration and is outside this course. The artist should decline on scope grounds, without suggesting where the service could be obtained, and should offer the temporary brow shaping and makeup that is on the approved list. The decline and the reason are recorded on the booking.

workedExamples.situation: A studio owner wants to add an airbrush tan to the menu, and believes the service is outside the rules because no skin is broken.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is a service that does not break the skin automatically in scope?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The first question is whether the service involves skin penetration, and that is answered by the service itself. The owner must then check the state or council position at the studio's location and record the source and date. The product's safety data sheet must also be held before the service is offered. Only when these answers are recorded can the service be added to the list.

equipmentAndPpe: Approved service list, held with the booking system or kit
Safety data sheet for each product on the list, on hand at each appointment
Record of the state, territory or council position for each location where services are offered

commonErrors.error: Offering a permanent or semi-permanent makeup service because the client asks for it and the artist has the pigment.
commonErrors.prevention: Those services involve skin penetration and are outside this course. Decline on scope grounds and record the decision.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a service is allowed everywhere because one council or one state permits it.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the position for the location where the service will be done, and record the source.

commonErrors.error: Adding a service to the menu before the owner has checked the products.
commonErrors.prevention: A service is added only after the safety data sheets, the location check and the list entry are all recorded.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Permanent makeup, semi-permanent makeup, tattooing and injectable cosmetic treatments are outside this course. This lesson does not give authority to offer any of them, in any state or territory.

Victoria: the Department of Health states that temporary make-up application businesses must follow the 2019 infection prevention and control guideline for hair, beauty, tattooing and skin penetration industries. The text of that guideline was not read for this draft. UNCONFIRMED: the guideline's full requirements for make-up application.

Registration, licence and council classification for makeup-related services differ by state, territory and council. UNCONFIRMED in this draft: the position for each jurisdiction. Check the source for the location before offering a service.

qualityStandard: Every service offered is on the approved list, with a review date
No skin-penetration or injectable service is offered, advertised or described as available under this course
The location position for each service is recorded with its source and date
documentationEvidence: Approved service list with review date
Scope check record for each new service, with the source and date
Declined-request record for each out-of-scope service, with the reason
summary: Permanent makeup, semi-permanent makeup, tattooing and injectables are outside this course
Victoria's Department of Health requires temporary make-up application businesses to follow the 2019 infection prevention and control guideline
Registration and licence positions vary by state, territory and council, and must be checked and recorded for each location

knowledgeChecks.question: Which of these services is outside this course?
options: Event makeup applied with a product from a sealed, labelled pot
Semi-permanent eyebrow pigment placed into the skin
Bridal makeup applied at the client's home

knowledgeChecks.question: A student is asked to offer a new service. Which step comes first?
options: Order the products that the service will need
Set the price and publish it on the website
Check whether the service involves skin penetration or injection

knowledgeChecks.question: In Victoria, what does the Department of Health say about temporary make-up application businesses?
options: They must follow the 2019 infection prevention and control guideline for hair, beauty, tattooing and skin penetration industries
They need no guideline, because makeup does not break the skin
They must follow only the product manufacturer's label
